title: Multiplication
description: Class 3 IMO — Multiplication as repeated addition, tables 2 to 10, multiplying 2- and 3-digit numbers by 1-digit, 2-digit by 2-digit, and word problems.

topics.title: Repeated Addition & Tables
topics.concept:
Multiplication is a short way to add equal groups. 4 groups of 6 = 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24, written as 4 × 6 = 24. The order does not matter: 4 × 6 = 6 × 4.

Knowing the tables from 2 to 10 makes multiplication fast. For example, the table of 7 is 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56, 63, 70.
recap: Order does not matter: a × b = b × a.

topics.title: Multiplying by a 1-digit Number
topics.concept:
To multiply a 2- or 3-digit number by a 1-digit number, multiply the Ones first, then the Tens, then the Hundreds, carrying when a product is 10 or more.

For 34 × 3: ones 3 × 4 = 12 (write 2, carry 1), tens 3 × 3 = 9, plus carry 1 = 10, so the answer is 102.
recap: Multiply Ones, then Tens, then Hundreds.
Carry to the next place when a product is 10 or more.

topics.title: Multiplying 2-digit by 2-digit & Word Problems
topics.concept:
To multiply two 2-digit numbers, split the second number into tens and ones, multiply each part, then add. For 23 × 12: 23 × 2 = 46 and 23 × 10 = 230, so 46 + 230 = 276.

In word problems, look for equal groups — rows, packets, dozens — and multiply.

examples.problem: A box has 25 pens. How many pens in 6 boxes?

recap: Split the second number into tens and ones, multiply, then add.
Word problems with equal groups use multiplication.

quiz.q: A shelf holds 13 books. How many books on 12 such shelves?

questions.q: One dozen = 12. How many bananas in 5 dozen?
A book costs ₹45. How much do 6 books cost?
A hall has 8 rows with 9 chairs in each. How many chairs in all?
An auditorium has 15 rows of 12 seats. How many seats in total?
Each car carries 4 tyres on the wheels and 1 spare. How many tyres for 23 cars?
questions.explanation: Each car has 5 tyres, so 23 × 5 = 115 tyres.
